artifacts.summary: Derives Check J's in-scope criterion by mechanically probing all 81 dispatchable agent files against its own section-locating logic (44 writers, 23 never-write-one research agents, 8 forked-subagent-only exclusions, zero misclassified); identifies the matching convention as the EXCLUDED-style curated array (Checks E/F/N), not the INCLUDED-style one (Checks C/G/H/M); shows the fail-closed-by-default redesign needs no bolted-on completeness-net check; and traces the 'dispatch-derived predicate' idea's full history (completed via archived task 212 for a different file, not rejected on merit, and structurally inapplicable to a static markdown lint).

memory_candidates.content: When designing a curated-array lint check in lint-agent-contracts.sh (or similar), first measure the true population shape (what fraction of the population is in-scope) before picking INCLUDED-style (Checks C/G/H/M: small hand-picked subset, needs a bolted-on completeness-net check like Check N to catch silent omission) vs EXCLUDED-style (Checks E/F/N's own exclusion arrays: almost-everyone minus a few named exceptions, fails loud by default on a new unregistered member -- no completeness net needed). The failure direction inverts between the two shapes: INCLUDED-style omits silently, EXCLUDED-style (iterating the full enumerate_dispatchable_agents() universe directly) fails loudly. Prefer EXCLUDED-style whenever the measured shape supports it.

A 'replace allowlist X with a dispatch-derived predicate' design that succeeded for one script (orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh's is_contractual_handoff_writer -> --handoff-expected flag, task 212) does not automatically transfer to a different script with a superficially similar allowlist. The mechanism only works where a live dispatch row exists to derive the predicate from; a static lint over markdown files at lint time has no dispatch context, so 'dispatch-derived' is a category error there -- the correct analog is a role/filename/content-derived curated classification instead.

lint-agent-contracts.sh's Check N completeness-net glob '*implementation*agent.md' does not match the '*-implement-agent.md' naming variant (epi-implement-agent.md, founder-implement-agent.md); CHECK_G_EXCLUDED_RELATIVE_PATHS lists epi-implement-agent.md as an exclusion but Check N's own glob never reaches it, making that entry dead code. Any future completeness-net-style check in this file should source its base universe from enumerate_dispatchable_agents() (frontmatter-based, already handles both naming suffixes correctly) rather than inventing a fresh filename glob.
